notes.title: Welcome New Players!
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

This is just a quick message to say welcome and thank you to all the new players who have added the game to their libraries since it went free to play.

You've absolutely blown me away with how many of you there are. Over 5000 new players in the first two days is crazy! It's amazing to see so many people enjoying the game and even submitting levels to the workshop so I just wanted to send out a quick thanks to everyone.

That being said, we still haven't hit 10 reviews yet which means the game isn't anywhere near as visible on the steam store as it would be with just a couple more reviews, so if you are enjoying the game it would make a massive difference to just spend those 30 seconds leaving a review for the game.

Once the game hits 10 reviews and gets a review score we can probably double that number of new players so i'd really REALLY appreciate anyone taking the time to leave a review.

Have a great halloween!  

- Nutter

notes.title: Patch 1.03 is now live!
notes.content:
[b]Hi everyone![/b]

As promised patch 1.03 is here and with it comes the release of the new Outbreak! Level pack as well as the free to play release of the base game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42512461/d8da94f2c215e162d683417559da0fafe3bb908e.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42512461/aa7954d436168247339946a30dbdfe17c8f7062b.png[/img]

Blobbs: Outbreak! is a brand new level pack i've been working on over the last 6 months or so and offers a whole new 70* levels of zombie filled puzzles to solve, just in time for halloween.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42512461/9cb82ef8737933d4bd93961f212da01e2254c658.png[/img]

For the first time in the Blobbs series, this level pack also features a branching storyline where you can choose to either stop the outbreak by helping researchers research a cure for the infected blobbs, or take the more aggressive option and join the military destroy the outbreak with as much firepower as they can muster.

With this branch in the story, the level pack has a total of 70 levels and two different versions of the final boss so needless to say it's definitely been most complicated level pack developed for the game so far.

[b]But that's not the only big news of this update![/b]

Today the (base) game has gone free to play, which hopefully means we'll be welcoming a whole (zombie) horde of new players who can now pick up the game (including the Reloaded level pack) for free. 

As a special thank you to all the legacy players who already purchased the game between since it's released in 2022, right up to today when it has gone free to play. I will be adding the Elemental Mayhem DLC, Mad Science DLC and the NEW Outbreak! DLC to the legacy package. Which to put it in simple terms, means that if you didn't already own Mad Science or Elemental Science, you'll be getting them for free along with all legacy players recieving a free copy of the new Outbreak level pack. Thanks again for giving Blobbs: Remastered a shot and for supporting a small indie dev!

Have a great halloween and I hope you enjoy tackling the zombie threat in Blobbs: Outbreak whichever way you choose to deal with it!

- Nutter

notes.title: Blobbs Remastered is going free to play!
notes.content:
[b]Hi everyone![/b]

So there's a lot of news to cover with this post so lets start with the big one!

[h3]Blobbs Remastered is going free to play![/h3]
Now just to be clear, when I say the Blobbs Remastered is going free to play, i'm referring to the base game, specifically the 50 levels that make up the Reloaded level pack. The Elemental Mayhem and Mad Science level packs, along with the new one i'll be revealing in this update post will still be (optional) paid content.

[u][b]Why go free to play and why now?[/b][/u]
To be totally upfront and honest with you all, Blobbs hasn't really taken off. It's sold quite a few copies, more than I expected if i'm honest, but certainly not enough to make back all of it's development costs. And that's totally okay, I make these games as a hobby for the most part and i'm lucky enough that i'll still be able to keep doing it even if my next game doesn't sell a million copies. [strike]Microsoft[/strike] A publisher isn't going to be shutting me down for failing to meet expectations. 

Really I make these games to provide a bit of fun and entertainment to people and it's always a shame when the number of people who actually see and get to experience the games is so small. But as some of you may remember, Retro Vaders: Reloaded (my first release on Steam) was free to play from the outset and has literally a thousand times more downloads/installs than Blobbs does. 

Put simply, I want to give more people a chance to experience the game, and i'm hoping that removing the upfront cost might persuade more people to give it a try.

As a side note, the game only has 6 reviews right now which is really hurting visibility. If we could even get that up to just 10 reviews, the game would immediately start being shown to more people on steam so i'd really REALLY appreciate it if anyone could spend 5 minutes dropping a quick review of the game. It really does make all the difference!

[u][b]But what about the people who already paid for the game?[/b][/u]
A great question, and obviously I appreciate every single person who has already given Blobbs a try, even more so that they were willing to spend some of their hard earned money on doing so. The last thing I'd ever want to do is make those people feel like they've been cheated out of their money because they bought the game before it went free to play.
 So here's what i'm planning to do... [b]When the game goes free to play, any person who currently owns the game will recieve Blobbs: Elemental Mayhem, Blobbs: Mad Science and the new level pack for free[/b]. You won't need to do anything, they will just be added to your account as part of the Legacy paid package you already own. 

But with that out of the way... I should probably actually reveal the new level pack right!? 

Introducing... 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42512461/d8da94f2c215e162d683417559da0fafe3bb908e.png[/img]

Coming this Halloween, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2499340/Blobbs_Outbreak]Blobbs: Outbreak[/url] is a new level pack which introduces new Infected, Infectious and even Zombie Blobbs to the game. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42512461/aa7954d436168247339946a30dbdfe17c8f7062b.png[/img]
Patch 1.02 teased it a little bit with Infectious Blobbs and Vaccine Blobbs being added to the level editor, but this level pack dials up the zombie fun to 11. Not only that, but for the first time in the Blobbs series, it even has a branching story with two totally different level paths and different endings depending on which path you choose during your playthrough.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42512461/9cb82ef8737933d4bd93961f212da01e2254c658.png[/img]
Choose the Cure path and work alongside researchers, testing vaccines as you try to develop a cure before it's too late!
Or choose the Destroy path and fight alongside the military, using all the firepower they can muster to contain and eradicate the source of the outbreak. 

Each branch of the level pack plays out totally differently, with the Cure path having more puzzle solving elements whilst the Destroy path is all about the gratituous blobb exploding we all know and love. It means that in total, this level pack actually has 70 levels instead of 50, along with two different versions of the final boss, depending on which branch of the story you're on. A lot of work has gone into this level pack and i'm excited to share it with all of you.

You may have also noticed a small patch which has released alongside this post. Not huge changes at this time, but it adds a new page to the DLC screen with some more information about outbreak and a button to wishlist (or eventually buy) the level pack in the same way you can with Elemental Mayhem and Mad Science. Once we get to October you'll see a few more changes like this, adding a second page for more (new) achievements, etc. But i'll cover that in more detail in another post closer to the date.

Phew! We got there... I know that's a lot of information to process and this news post is already crazy long... so i'll leave it there. Leave a comment if anything about the giveaway for legacy players is unclear and i'll do my best to answer any questions or concerns.

- Nutter

notes.title: Patch 1.02 is now live!
notes.content:
[b]Hi everyone![/b]

It's been a little while since there was any Blobbs related news on here, but whilst it might have seemed like i'd just released the game and vanished after patch 1.01a, i've actually been quietly working away on some new stuff which I hope to reveal later in the year.

For now, i'm releasing Patch 1.02 which fixes a few issues I noticed and adds functionality for the new stuff. Most of it is under the hood that you probably shouldn't even notice, but here's a list of changes for anyone interested.

[h3]Bug Fixes:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed Green Blobbs not being able to be spawned in the level editor (and possibly other places) on April 20th (due an unanticipated side-effect of the 4/20 Easter Egg). 
[*] Fixed an issue with the Music Player which was sometimes causing new tracks to start before the previous one finished.
[/list]
[h3]New Additions:[/h3]
Two new types of Blobbs have been added to the Level Editor, consider these a teaser of new content coming later in the year,
(Spoilers Ahead)
Infectious Blobbs - [spoiler] which release a noxious gas which can infect (some) other types of Blobbs, transforming them into Infected variants.[/spoiler] 
Vaccine Blobbs - [spoiler] which release a cloud of inoculating mist which will revert infected blobbs back into their original form and vaccinate uninfected blobbs to prevent them from getting infected.[/spoiler] 
Infected Variants of Basic Blobbs -[spoiler]Green, Blue, Red, Yellow, Orange & Purple Blobbs can now become infected, and will spread the infection further they if are exploded before they get cured.[/spoiler] 

[h3]Misc Updates & General Improvements:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Reworked the functionality of cosmetic variations to better support "theming" how the blobbs look without having to make an entire new version of that blobb. (This also identified and then subsequently helped fix the 4/20 Bug).
[*] Updated the Level Selection screen and level pack selection logic to simplify/streamline adding new official level packs in the future [i](hint hint)[/i]
[*] Added functionality (currently un-used in this patch) to allow for multiple "pages" on certain screens (such as the achievements screen) so more can be added in the future without having to cram it all into one page.
[/list]

It doesn't look like much when it's just bullet points on the patch notes, but a whole lot of work has been going on behind the scenes to future proof the game and make it possible to add additional level packs, more crazy blobb types and even more achievements to unlock. I'm really looking forward to sharing more news about new content in the coming months, talk soon!

- Nutter

notes.title: Patch 1.01 is now live!
notes.content:
[b]Hey everyone![/b]

It's been just short of two weeks since the game launched as the dust has just about settled. It appears I was lucky enough to have not missed any major bugs in the 1.00 release which makes this 1.01 patch pretty minor in terms of bug fixes.

The one thing this patch will improve however, is the difficulty of a few of the levels in the Remastered, Mad Science and Elemental Mayhem level packs. Whilst I did intend for the difficulty of levels to ramp up and become more challenging as you progressed through each level pack, there are a few stand out levels where the difficulty "spiked" a little too much and created a lot of frustration for some players.

Obviously we play games to have fun, and whilst a little challenge can still be fun, banging your head against a wall over and over because a level is frustratingly difficult isn't most people's idea of fun (myself included). That being the case, a selection of levels have had a few changes to make them a little less difficult/frustrating to complete.

[h3]The Following levels have been changed:[/h3]

[b]Remastered Level Pack[/b]
[list]
[*] Level 30 (Ghostbusting) - Increased the number of Ghost Blobbs in the level to 9.
[*] Level 41 (Chaos Mastery) - Increased the number of Chaos Blobbs in the level to 14 (and adjusted the level target accordingly).
[*] Level 44 (Gravity Well) - Increased the number of Blackhole Blobbs in the level to 7.
[*] Level 46 (Crossing the Streams) - Increased the number of starting clicks from 1 to 2.
[*] Level 47 (Feeling Blue) - Increased the number of starting clicks from 4 to 5.
[/list]
[b]Elemental Mayhem Level Pack[/b]
[list]
[*] Level 7 (Crippling Cold) - Increased the number of Ghost Blobbs in the level to 9.
[*] Level 9 (Deep Freeze) - Increased the number of Purple Blobbs in the level to 8.
[*] Level 11 (Thawing Out) - Increased the number of Green Blobbs in the level to 15.
[*] Level 18 (Heatwave) - Increased the number of Blaze Blobbs in the level to 10.
[*] Level 26 (Cooling Down) - Increased the number of Green Blobbs in the level to 15.
[*] Level 28 (Bright Spark) - Increased the number of Blue Blobbs in the level to 5.
[*] Level 36 (Stormcaller) - Increased the starting number of clicks from 1 to 2.
[*] Level 46 (Elemental Evolution) - Increased the number of Blue Blobbs in the level to 13 and the number of Frosty Blobbs in the level to 2.
[*] Level 47 (Fall to Tyranny) - Increased the starting number of clicks from 1 to 2.
[/list]
[b]Mad Science Level Pack[/b]
[list]
[*] Level 2 (Spot the Difference) - Made the "missing" assistant [i]slightly[/i] more obvious.
[*] Level 3 (Definitely Impossible... Right?) - Increased the number of Green Blobbs in the level to 18.
[*] Level 4 (What a Mess!) - Increased the number of Chaos Blobbs in the level to 3.
[*] Level 7 (Molecular Decomposition) Increased the starting number of clicks from 2 to 3.
[*] Level 11 (Pursuit of Knowledge) - Increased the Number of Tiny Blobbs in the level to 5 (and adjusted the Level target accordingly)
[*] Level 13 (A (W)hole new species) - Increased the number of Tiny Blobbs in the level to 25.
[*] Level 18 (Meet the Chargebot) - Adjusted the level description to explain the mechanics of the Chargebot more clearly.
[/list]
These changes should make some of the more frustrating levels a little easier and make the difficulty curves throughout the level packs feel more gradual and less spiky.

[u][b]Please consider leaving a review of the game![/b][/u]
Finally to close out this update post, a small ask from me. Without reviews and player feedback I wouldn't have been able to identify which levels were becoming frustrating and I wouldn't have been able to improve those levels in this patch. Player feedback really does help and really does matter. If you've enjoyed the game so far please consider leaving a positive review to help the game grow and gain visibility. Likewise if a level really annoyed you, leave a review about that too and let me know so I can look to try improve it in patch 1.02. 

For a small indie dev like myself with almost no marketing budget, word of mouth and positive reviews are absolutely crucial in the game having a chance of getting noticed and with just 2 reviews (at the time of writing this post), the game has almost [b]zero[/b] visibility on Steam outside of people who wishlisted it before launch. 

It doesn't take long to leave a review, and it certainly doesn't need to be a sprawling essay, but if just a fraction of the people who have already bought the game took a few minutes to leave a quick review we could easily hit the 10+ reviews threshold where Steam starts to showcase the game to more people.

Thanks and enjoy the game!

- Nutter
